about.title: Four and five
about.length_note: About 10 minutes. The class has two short parts, counting 4 and 5, then the five-frame. You can stop after any beat and pick up there next time. If you want a longer session, repeat the 'how many?' questions with different things from around you.

say.text: Welcome back. Today we count up to five. There is no hurry, and you can stop at any point.

show.text: Four and five

say.text: If you can, find some real things to touch. Grown-ups might use cups, keys or coins. Children might use apples, balls or toy ducks. If you have nothing nearby, the pictures work well too.

show.text:
Cups, keys, coins
Ducks, apples, balls
Or just the pictures

say.text: First, a warm-up. Touch each cup once as you count: one, two, three.

show.text: Three blue cups in a row on a table, each one large and clear.

ask.why: Touch each cup once and say one, two, three. The last number you say is the answer: 3.

say.text: Now add one more cup. Touch each cup once and count along: one, two, three, four. The last number you say tells you how many. That number is four.
Let's try it with apples. Count them slowly, touching each one.

show.text: Four red apples in a row.

ask.why: One, two, three, four. There are 4 apples.

say.text: This is the word four, and this is the digit 4. Say it with me: four.

show.text: four  (4)

say.text: Add one more thing. One, two, three, four, five. Five coins. You are now counting up to five.
Here are some ducks. Point to each duck as you count.

show.text: Five yellow ducks in a row.

ask.why: One, two, three, four, five. There are 5 ducks.

say.text: This is the word five, and this is the digit 5. Say it with me: five.

show.text: five  (5)

say.text: Now a helpful tool, called a five-frame. It is a row of five boxes. Each box holds one thing.

show.text: A row of five empty square boxes, side by side, drawn with thick outlines.

say.text: We fill the boxes one at a time, from the left. One. Two. Three. Four. Five.

show.text: The same row of five boxes. A red counter appears in each box in turn, from left to right.

say.text: When every box is full, that is five. You don't need to count again. A full five-frame means 5.

show.text: A five-frame with all five boxes full of red counters, and a large 5 beside it.

say.text: Now take one counter away. Four boxes are full and one is empty. One empty box means four. Four is just one short of five.

show.text: A five-frame with four boxes full of red counters and the last box empty, and a large 4 beside it.

say.text: Look at the frame. You can count the counters, or you can notice the empty box.

show.text: A five-frame with four boxes full and one box empty.

ask.q: How many counters are in the frame?
ask.why: Four boxes are full and one is empty. That is 4.

say.text: Here is another frame.

show.text: A five-frame with all five boxes full.

ask.q: How many counters are in the frame?
ask.why: There are no empty boxes. A full five-frame means 5.

say.text: Let's match the frames to the digits. Look at the left side, then the right.

show.text:
Frame with 4 full boxes and 1 empty box | 4
Frame with all 5 boxes full | 5

say.text: Listen to the word, then choose the digit. Five.

show.text: five

ask.why: The word five goes with the digit 5.

say.text: Now a mixed round, with numbers from one to five. Take your time with each one.

show.text: Two silver keys on a table.

say.text: Next one.

show.text: Five orange balls in a row.

ask.why: Count them one at a time: one, two, three, four, five. There are 5 balls.

say.text: And another. This time the coins are in a five-frame.

show.text: A five-frame with four gold coins in the first four boxes and the last box empty.

ask.why: One box is empty, so it is one less than five. That is 4.

say.text: One more.

show.text: One green apple on its own.

ask.why: There is just one apple. That is 1.

say.text: Well done. This is a good place to rest if you need to. Everyone learns at their own speed, and coming back to it another day helps too.

show.text: Good work. Rest here if you like.

say.text: To remember: four is a five-frame with one empty box. Five is a full five-frame. In the next class we meet zero, which is when there is nothing there at all.

show.text:
4 = four full boxes, one empty
5 = a full five-frame
Next time: zero
